task.description: WF-01 Step 2 HARD GATE: validate the 18 new S3 requirements REQ-043..REQ-060 that REQ-ANALYST appended to docs/requirements.yaml, plus its rewrite of docs/migration/stage-3-instance-engine.md. Run checks a-e from WF-01 Step 2 against EVERY one of the 18 -- TESTABILITY, CONSISTENCY, DEPENDS_ON CORRECTNESS, STAGE FIT, SIZE -- and report per-requirement, not in aggregate. ORCH has already independently verified the purely structural properties, so do NOT spend your effort re-deriving these (they are confirmed true): schema completeness on all 18, zero duplicate ids, zero orphaned depends_on, >=4 acceptance criteria each, zero dependency cycles, and append-only (git diff shows requirements.yaml has literally zero removed lines). Your job is the SEMANTIC checks those structural ones cannot catch.
acceptance_criteria: TESTABILITY (check a): every acceptance criterion across all 18 requirements is one a test could definitively pass or fail. Flag vague wording ('appropriately', 'as needed', 'reasonably', 'correctly handles') per requirement id and criterion index. Pay attention to criteria that assert moduledoc TEXT content -- those are testable and acceptable (REQ-040 set that precedent), but criteria asserting a design QUALITY are not

CONSISTENCY (check b): read all four docs/migration/decisions/*.md records in full plus the shipped S2 requirements the S3 entries build on, and confirm no S3 requirement contradicts a decision record or a done requirement. Specifically verify: tenant-scoping via REQ-022's schema-per-tenant mechanism is applied consistently to new S3 tables (or a GLOBAL exception is explicitly flagged as an OPEN QUESTION the way REQ-041 did), and 0001-web-framework's Plug/Bandit-not-Phoenix decision is not quietly contradicted

DEPENDS_ON CORRECTNESS (check c): not just non-orphaned (already confirmed) but GENUINELY required and sufficient. Verify the claimed chain shape actually holds -- REQ-043+REQ-044 are the two independent roots, REQ-045 converges them, REQ-052 is the reconvergence point, REQ-059->060 closes the pin chain. Look hard for MISSING dependencies: a requirement that in practice cannot start until another has shipped but does not cite it. Two specific ones to check: does REQ-048 (complete task) really need REQ-049 (variable merge) rather than the reverse, and should REQ-051's parallel join cite REQ-043's tokens table more directly?

STAGE FIT (check d): every one of the 18 is genuinely S3 instance-engine scope. Confirm the stated S4 boundary (no HTTP routes/controllers -- engine functions return tagged tuples and leave status mapping to S4) and the S5 boundary (no Lua/WASM runtime -- REQ-057 keeps only the registry contract, REQ-058 only the audit persistence path and explicitly forbids adding a Lua/NIF dependency to mix.exs) are actually honoured in the requirement TEXT, not just asserted in the summary. Also confirm REQ-058 does not depend on an S5 deliverable that does not exist yet

SIZE (check e): each of the 18 is plausibly one agent turn. This is the check most likely to fail -- R-Co's instance.zig is 5,550 lines split across only six requirements and transition.zig is 3,323 across three. For each requirement, judge honestly whether it smuggles multiple unrelated deliverables. REQ-051 (parallel split AND join, EE-06+EE-07 -- two separate R-Co requirements in one entry) and REQ-052 (cancellation AND execution error handling, EE-08+EE-10 -- likewise two) are the two most likely oversized entries; scrutinise both specifically and say whether each should be split

Verify REQ-ANALYST's deferral claims are accurate rather than convenient, by checking them against R-Co's actual source: that transition_source_embed.zig genuinely has no Elixir-meaningful behavior to port (read the file), and that PIN-01 AC1/AC2 and PIN-03 AC3 are genuinely unsatisfiable today because service_catalog and PLC-01 do not exist (R-Co's own pin_resolver.zig header states this scoping -- confirm it, and confirm REQ-059 carries the limitation forward with typed errors rather than silently dropping the ACs)

Verify the OPEN QUESTION flags are genuine deferrals to CODE-DESIGNER and not requirement-text hedging that hides an untestable acceptance criterion. Specifically: REQ-045's process-vs-row question (the stage's largest), REQ-052's cancellation-of-a-live-process, REQ-054's snapshot cadence, REQ-057's registry storage, REQ-043's tokens-table-necessity, and REQ-050's condition-evaluator build/adopt question. For REQ-050 in particular, assess whether an evaluator with NO reference implementation to port (R-Co's vendor/cel/cel.zig is reportedly a stub and REQ-029 shipped syntax-checking only) is safely expressible as a requirement or genuinely needs a decision record FIRST -- if it needs one, that is a legitimate FAIL-worthy finding

Confirm stage-3-instance-engine.md's rewrite preserved both Early findings (idiomatic gen_statem/supervision bar; process-per-instance is not the default) rather than paraphrasing them away, and that its REVIEWER sign-off section was not fabricated with sign-offs that never happened

Report PASS or FAIL. Any FAIL must cite the specific requirement id AND which check letter (a-e) failed, per WF-01 Step 2. Partial credit is not a valid outcome -- if any requirement fails any check, the gate result is FAIL with the specific rework list

result.summary: RE-GATE PASS (rework iteration 1). Batch grew from 18 to 20 requirements (REQ-043..REQ-062). All three iteration-0 blocking findings and both minors are resolved and independently verified against R-Co source: REQ-050's false 'no reference implementation' premise corrected to port transition.zig:1118's evaluateGatewayCondition() plus src/expr/ (with the stale-text warning propagated to the stage doc, and REQ-ANALYST's additional finding that engine.md L451/L1005/L1020 carry the same stale wording confirmed); REQ-052 split into REQ-052 (EE-08, 658 design-doc lines) and REQ-061 (EE-10, 666), both at the REQ-044 baseline of 644; and REQ-062 added to close REQ-032's deferred SPC-01 runtime half, with all seven of its instance.zig/transition.zig line citations verified exact and the GH #428 token-copy bug turned into a required regression test. All rewired dependency edges checked semantically and correct, including REQ-058's repoint to REQ-045. REQ-051 correctly left unsplit. The append-order concern REQ-ANALYST raised is cosmetic: both the queue and the single-host fallback gate on depends_on satisfaction before file order. Full per-iteration detail in result.gate_history. Requirements ready for WF-02.

gate_history.summary: HARD GATE FAIL. Checks a-e run per requirement against all 18 (REQ-043..REQ-060), verified against R-Co source rather than REQ-ANALYST's self-report. 15 of 18 pass all five checks and are high quality: zero vague-wording hits across every acceptance criterion (check a clean on all 18), every cited S2 dependency confirmed status:done, every src/design/engine.md line citation (L18/442/1086/1632/2238/2638/2898/3299/3957/4571/5237/5771) verified exact, REQ-043's claim about REQ-023's migration header verified verbatim against priv/repo/migrations/20260816120003_create_instance_projections.exs, and no contradiction found with 0001 (Phoenix/Plug -- S3 text consistently defers routes to S4, never contradicts) or 0003 (schema-per-tenant applied to all five new tables with correct tenant_id-derived-from-prefix per the Addendum). Three FAIL findings block the gate. (1) REQ-050 check b CONSISTENCY -- its load-bearing factual premise is FALSE. It asserts 'R-Co's own vendor/cel/cel.zig is a STUB' and therefore 'Letflow has NO reference implementation to port'. vendor/cel/cel.zig is a 13,877-byte working subset evaluator with tokenizer, recursive-descent parser, and `pub fn evaluate()` at line 391; R-Co's own EE-05 entry lists it under implemented_in. Production evaluation additionally moved to src/expr/ (7 files, ~195KB: lexer/parser/ast/evaluator), reached from transition.zig via evaluateGatewayCondition() at transition.zig:1118 -- a complete, directly portable reference for EE-05's exact semantics including the catch-false-on-error rule REQ-050 AC3 needs. The 'stub' wording is stale text in R-Co's src/design/definition.md:1143 describing a state retired by commit 480b7dc5; REQ-029 correctly quoted it as R-Co documentation in a definition-time syntax-check context, but REQ-050 propagated it as a current fact about runtime evaluation without reading the file. This inverts the requirement's framing from a translation into a build/adopt decision and would send CODE-DESIGNER to a decision record it does not need. This is a wrong-premise defect, not a missing decision record. (2) REQ-052 check e SIZE -- genuinely oversized, split required. It bundles EE-08 cancellation and EE-10 execution error handling, two separate RELEASED R-Co requirements with disjoint acceptance-criteria sets, distinct callers, and separate design-doc sections totalling 1,324 lines of engine.md (EE-08 658 + EE-10 666) -- double the largest single-section requirement in the batch and 2x REQ-044's EE-02 (644). It additionally carries a third deliverable (superseding lib/letflow/parallel_approval.ex + ApprovalSupervisor), three out-of-scope hooks, and an OPEN QUESTION, across 7 acceptance criteria. The stated justification (shared locking/guard structure) does not hold: EE-08 is caller-initiated and drives to CANCELLED terminal, EE-10 is engine-internal, driven by REQ-049/050/056/057 failure paths, and halts at ERROR non-terminally pending an S6 DLQ operator action. It is also the reconvergence point (depends_on REQ-048/050/051) with five downstream requirements, so oversizing here has the widest blast radius in the stage. Contrast REQ-051 (EE-06+EE-07, 661 lines combined -- comparable to REQ-044's single section): that pairing is CORRECTLY sized and should NOT be split, since split and join share the Token/JoinCounter model and R-Co's EE-07 AC2/AC3 cancelled-branch-exclusion rule is unstateable without the split. (3) REQ-032's deferred SPC-01 half is MISSING from the batch entirely -- a check c coverage gap at batch level. REQ-032 (done, S2) states in its own text and acceptance criterion 5 that SPC-01 (runtime sub-process activation/completion helpers) 'is explicitly OUT of this requirement's scope -- it belongs to S3', naming src/engine/instance.zig as its future integration point. SPC-01 is RELEASED in R-Co and implemented across instance.zig (startSubProcessesForPendingEventsInTx, createWithParentInheritance, computeChildInitialVariables, and the four SUB_PROCESS interface-contract errors at instance.zig:258-270/4147/4524) -- squarely inside this stage's src/engine/ scope. No requirement among the 18 ports it, and stage-3-instance-engine.md never mentions SPC-01 or sub-processes at all, so it is dropped silently rather than deferred explicitly. Two of the 18 depend on it existing: REQ-044 ports Token's waiting_child_instance_id field (meaningful only for sub-processes) and REQ-059's AC6 requires child-instance pin inheritance with source:inherited, which presupposes a child-instance creation path nothing in the batch builds. Deferral-honesty checks all PASS and are recorded as accurate rather than convenient: transition_source_embed.zig verified to be a 24-line @embedFile shim for a Zig module-root constraint with no Elixir-meaningful behavior (correctly given no requirement); PIN-01 AC1/AC2 and PIN-03 AC3 verified genuinely unsatisfiable -- pin_resolver.zig's own header states the identical scoping including the ISS-0672/GH-306 tracking id, and REQ-059 correctly carries typed UnresolvedCatalogRef/UnresolvedModuleRef errors forward rather than dropping the ACs; REQ-058's narrowness statement verified verbatim against lua_script_audit.zig's header including the three src/lua/ imports and the supersedes-rather-than-extends language, with mix.exs-no-Lua-dependency correctly enforced as an acceptance criterion. REQ-048's depends_on [REQ-047, REQ-049] verified CORRECT in the direction ORCH queried -- engine.md's EE-04 algorithm merges variables inside completeTask's transaction, so REQ-049 genuinely must precede REQ-048, not the reverse. REQ-051's depends_on need not add REQ-043: it is a pure in-memory transition requirement (Token/JoinCounter values), and its persistence is REQ-047's job, which already carries REQ-043 transitively via REQ-045. Stage doc verified: both Early findings preserved substantively (not paraphrased away) and the REVIEWER sign-off section honestly reads '(None yet -- this stage hasn't started.)' rather than being fabricated; its only defect is propagating REQ-050's false CEL claim at lines 153-156, which must be corrected alongside finding (1). Two MINOR non-blocking issues also recorded for the rework pass.
issues: FAIL REQ-050 check b (CONSISTENCY): asserts R-Co's vendor/cel/cel.zig is a stub with 'NO reference implementation to port'. False -- cel.zig is a 13,877-byte working evaluator with pub fn evaluate() at line 391 (and is named in R-Co's own EE-05 implemented_in), while current production evaluation lives in src/expr/ (7 files, ~195KB) reached via transition.zig's evaluateGatewayCondition() at line 1118. The 'stub' phrasing is stale text in R-Co src/design/definition.md:1143, retired by commit 480b7dc5. Rework: reframe the OPEN QUESTION from build/adopt to port-src/expr-semantics-vs-adopt-a-hex-library, and correct the identical claim in docs/migration/stage-3-instance-engine.md lines 153-156.

FAIL REQ-052 check e (SIZE): bundles EE-08 (658 design-doc lines) and EE-10 (666) = 1,324, double the batch's largest single-section requirement, plus a third deliverable (superseding parallel_approval.ex + ApprovalSupervisor), three out-of-scope hooks and an OPEN QUESTION across 7 acceptance criteria. The shared-locking justification does not hold -- EE-08 is caller-initiated and terminal-CANCELLED, EE-10 is engine-internal and non-terminal-ERROR with different callers. Split into REQ-052 (EE-08 cancellation + the parallel_approval.ex supersession) and a new EE-10 requirement, rewiring the depends_on of REQ-053/056/057/058 which all reconverge here.

FAIL batch-level check c (DEPENDS_ON / coverage): REQ-032 (done) explicitly deferred SPC-01's runtime half to S3 naming src/engine/instance.zig as its integration point, but no requirement among REQ-043..REQ-060 ports it and stage-3-instance-engine.md never mentions sub-processes. SPC-01 is RELEASED in R-Co and implemented in the in-scope instance.zig (instance.zig:258-270, 559, 2053, 4147, 4524). REQ-044 ports Token.waiting_child_instance_id and REQ-059 AC6 requires child pin inheritance, both of which presuppose the missing path. Add an SPC-01 requirement (sub-process activation/completion, interface input/output contract enforcement, child-instance creation) or state an explicit, R-Co-grounded deferral in the stage doc the way transition_source_embed.zig was handled.

MINOR REQ-049 and REQ-059 both cite "REQ-024's validate_payload/2". The shipped function is validate_payload/3 (event_type, payload, tenant_id) in lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex:139; that module's own moduledoc records the /2 -> /3 arity change. Correct the arity in both descriptions so the implementer is not sent looking for a function that does not exist.

MINOR REQ-054 depends_on [REQ-053] only, but its acceptance criterion 4 requires reconstruction to replay from a snapshot -- i.e. it modifies REQ-053's reconstruct path. That is correct ordering, but the requirement should state that it EXTENDS REQ-053's shipped function rather than reading as a standalone module, so the implementer does not build a parallel reconstruct path.

gate_history.summary: RE-GATE after rework iteration 1: PASS. All three blocking findings and both minors from iteration 0 are resolved, verified against R-Co source rather than accepted from REQ-ANALYST's report. Batch is now 20 requirements (REQ-043..REQ-062). FINDING 1 RESOLVED (REQ-050 check b): the false 'no reference implementation' premise is gone and the requirement now ports R-Co's real implementation. Every new citation verified exact against source: evaluateGatewayCondition() at transition.zig:1118, vendor/cel/cel.zig at 13,877 bytes with pub fn evaluate() at line 391, all 7 src/expr/ filenames correct, and commit 480b7dc5 (wire src/expr into transition.zig; retire vendor/cel from production). REQ-ANALYST additionally found, and I independently confirmed, that the stale stub wording also sits in engine.md itself at L451 (stub; real implementation delivered separately), L1005 (evaluate TBD) and L1020 (OQ-3) -- a finding beyond my own, and material because engine.md is this stage's primary design reference. The four translateCelToExpr rewrite rules and the hasCelUnsupportedFeatures boundary match the source exactly, and catch-false is correctly identified as EE-05 AC4 itself rather than a second rule. Grew 6 -> 8 acceptance criteria, with the two additions (unsupported-feature catch-false, and direct testing of all four translation rewrites) both independently testable. The correction landed in all claimed places: requirements.yaml, and stage-3-instance-engine.md, which dropped REQ-050 from its decision-record candidates (three became two). On ORCH's question about warning future readers off engine.md's stale text -- the stage doc does carry that warning, and it is specific and durable: it names both files, the retiring commit, the byte size, and separates runtime from definition-time scope so REQ-029's correct quotation is not mistaken for a contradiction. That is adequate; no further action needed. The only remaining stub strings in docs/ are shipped REQ-029's own (line 1322, correctly untouched under append-only) and REQ-050's explanatory note about it (line 2609). FINDING 2 RESOLVED (REQ-052 check e): split into REQ-052 (EE-08 cancellation, 658 design-doc lines) and REQ-061 (EE-10 execution error handling, 666), each now at the REQ-044/EE-02 baseline of 644 and neither oversized. The boundary is drawn exactly where engine.md draws it (L3299 EE-08, L4571 EE-10), and both requirements articulate the kind-difference rather than merely the size one: EE-08 caller-initiated and terminal, EE-10 engine-internal and non-terminal pending an S6 operator action. REQ-052 kept the parallel_approval.ex supersession (correct -- it pairs with REQ-051's split/join) and gained a genuinely valuable new criterion requiring that an instance cancelled via REQ-051's all-branches-cancelled path and one cancelled directly reach the same persisted state. REQ-061 makes its shared-sink nature testable by requiring at least three of its five calling paths to demonstrably route into the one function, and correctly flags that ERROR is non-terminal in a way CANCELLED and COMPLETED are not. REQ-051 was correctly left unsplit per my iteration-0 finding. FINDING 3 RESOLVED (batch-level check c): REQ-062 closes the SPC-01 gap REQ-032 handed to S3. Every one of its line citations verified against R-Co source: the four-variant error enum at instance.zig:258-272, createWithParentInheritance at L562 including its verbatim 'never exposed on the public API surface' comment, startSubProcessesForPendingEventsInTx at L4668, buildSubProcessChildInitialVars at L4544, the SPC-01 code mapping at L4147-4155, the sub_process_completed handler at transition.zig:897, and the GH #428 token-copy bug comment at transition.zig:678. That last one is turned into a required regression test, which is the right call -- the bug silently strands a parent forever by dropping waiting_child_instance_id during token cloning, and it is exactly the class of defect that survives a naive test suite. The gap is genuinely closed for both dependents: REQ-044's Token.waiting_child_instance_id and REQ-059 AC6's child-instance pin inheritance now have the child-creation path they presupposed, with REQ-062 explicitly stating the seam against REQ-059 so neither re-implements the other's half. It also correctly ports R-Co's documented no-cascade behaviour (cancelling a parent does not cancel its child) rather than inventing one, and correctly notes there is no S4 endpoint to defer because sub-processes are engine-started. DEPENDENCY REWIRING verified edge by edge, semantically not just structurally. REQ-053 -> [REQ-052, REQ-061, REQ-026] is right: replay must reconstruct both CANCELLED and ERROR terminal states, and its criteria exercise the EXECUTION_ERROR replay path explicitly. REQ-056 and REQ-057 -> [REQ-061] are right: both route failure outcomes into the EE-10 sink and neither needs cancellation. REQ-058 -> [REQ-045] is right and the claim that its real dependency was always instance-start holds up: it only needs a valid instance_id to attribute an audit row to, never touches the ERROR path, so the original [REQ-052] edge was spurious. REQ-052 -> [REQ-048, REQ-051] correctly drops REQ-050 (gateway evaluation feeds the ERROR path, not cancellation) and keeps REQ-051 for the branch-cancellation interaction. REQ-061 -> [REQ-048, REQ-050] and REQ-062 -> [REQ-061, REQ-049, REQ-032] are both correct and sufficient. The seven prose repoints are right in both directions: every ERROR-path reference moved to REQ-061, and the single retained REQ-052 reference (REQ-051's join citing branches cancelled via EE-08) genuinely concerns cancellation and was correctly left. MINORS RESOLVED: REQ-049 now cites validate_payload/3 in both its description and its acceptance criterion. Leaving shipped REQ-024/REQ-025's own citations untouched was the correct call under append-only -- those entries are done, and REQ-024's module moduledoc already records the /2 -> /3 arity change, so a reader is not misled. My original REQ-059 flag needed no fix: it cites REQ-024's validator with no arity at all, so there was nothing to correct. REQ-054 now opens with an explicit THIS REQUIREMENT EXTENDS REQ-053's already-shipped reconstruct path -- it is not a standalone module statement. POSITIONAL-READ QUESTION (raised by REQ-ANALYST): cosmetic, no action needed. Nothing in this pipeline reads requirements.yaml positionally in a way REQ-061's file position could break. ORCHESTRATOR.md:46's single-host fallback selects the first pending requirement whose depends_on are all done, in file order -- file order is a tiebreaker applied AFTER the dependency filter, not a substitute for it, so an entry cannot be claimed before its dependencies are done regardless of position. TASK_QUEUE.md's get_next_task does the same filtering atomically and sequences by impl_order, which is assigned by register_task at scheduling time, not derived from file position. CHECKS a-e ON THE CHANGED SET (REQ-050, 052, 053, 054, 056, 057, 058, 059, 061, 062): all pass. Check a clean -- a fresh vague-wording sweep across all 20 returns a single hit, in REQ-052's prose rationale (was not sufficient justification), which is narrative, not an acceptance criterion. AC counts stay within 4-8 (6 to 8 across the changed set). Check b: no new contradiction with any decision record; the two new requirements add no schema surface, and REQ-062 reuses REQ-032's shipped parse/validate rather than introducing a second implementation. Check d: S4/S5 boundaries still honoured in requirement text -- REQ-061 defers the DLQ operator path to S6/S4, REQ-062 correctly states no HTTP surface exists to defer. Check e: both split halves and REQ-062 are each plausibly one agent turn. The ten requirements cleared in iteration 0 were not disturbed by the rework beyond the verified prose repoints. Gate result PASS; the 20 S3 requirements are ready for WF-02.
